text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Two Turks died in a boat carrying holidaymakers after it crashed into rocks and sunk close to a holiday resort near the western town of Mugla.
MILLIYET
- State ties with underworld gangs were brought to light during the testimonies of members of the intelligence services on trial in Istanbul's state security court.
- The minister for the economy suprised everyone with his statement that inflation will be 100 percent by year-end.
HURRIYET
- The cabinet accepted an eight-year compulsory education plan which they have now sent to parliament.
- The leader of junior coalition partner, the Democratic Turkey Party, says he expects more deputies to join the party.
YENI YUZYIL
- Washington has a high opinion of Turkey's new government and says it has established stability.
- The Fiat group and their Turkish partners Koc Holding will reveal an $262 million investment plan.
RADIKAL
- The environment minister supported villagers in the western town of Bergama in their fight against the Eurogold consortium's by suspending the company's mining plans.
CUMHURIYET
- The state minister responsible for human rights says he cannot guarantee the ending of the rights violations in Turkey.
DUNYA
- Turkish money has been weakest against the U.S. dollar in the past six years. One dollar reached 156,600 lira on Tuesday.
ZAMAN
- Former prime minister Tansu Ciller accuses the Turkish armed forces involvement in politics and calls it to withdraw.
